title: Spatial Memory Agent: Self-Improvement Without Touching the Weights
hook: A frozen VLM gets better at spatial reasoning by writing itself notes — verified lessons, scored by how well they transfer, retrieved at inference time.
key_points: Asks whether a frozen VLM can self-evolve at spatial reasoning without fine-tuning and without external depth or 3D tools at inference.
In a verifiable environment, SMA queries the frozen model, gets an answer plus a reward, then uses verifier-guided reflection to distill compact transferable lessons.
Each lesson carries a Transfer Reliability Score (TRS), initialized uniformly and recalibrated from whether later retrievals actually helped.
At deployment the memory is read-only: lessons are retrieved by semantic filter plus combined similarity–TRS ranking and injected to guide inference.
Across five spatial benchmarks and four base VLMs, SMA reports the highest macro average in every base-model block.
The pitch is a parameter-update-free path to improvement — memory as the learning substrate instead of gradients.
content_html: Two established routes exist for making a vision-language model better at spatial reasoning: post-train it (SFT, RL), or hand it external tools like depth estimators and 3D reconstruction at inference. Zhang and colleagues take a third path — leave the model frozen and give it a memory.
extra_html:
Spatial Memory Agent runs the frozen VLM inside a verifiable spatial environment, so each attempt yields both a prediction and a reward. Verifier-guided reflection then distills those episodes into compact, transferable lessons — the kind of note that generalizes rather than a cached answer. Each lesson gets a Transfer Reliability Score, initialized uniformly and then recalibrated by whether retrieving it later actually helped. At deployment the memory is read-only: incoming queries retrieve lessons through a semantic filter and a ranking that combines similarity with TRS, and the retrieved lessons steer the frozen model's inference.

Across five spatial benchmarks and four base VLMs, the authors report the highest macro average in every base-model block and the best accuracy in most of the 20 evaluations. The idea worth taking away is structural rather than numerical: if you can verify outcomes, you can accumulate capability in a retrieval store instead of in weights — cheaper to build, cheaper to audit, and easy to roll back. Whether the lessons keep transferring outside the benchmark families tested is the open question.

related.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill
related.hook: AutoMem treats knowing what to remember and when to retrieve it — metamemory — as a trainable skill, and tuning memory alone roughly doubles to quadruples performance on long-horizon games.

related.title: SpatialClaw: Code as the Action Interface for Spatial Reasoning
related.hook: Give a vision-language agent a live Python kernel instead of a fixed tool menu, and let it write one cell at a time. That flexibility lifts 3D/4D spatial reasoning by 11 points.

related.title: Concept-Guided Spatial Regularization for World Models in Atari Pong
related.hook: Five world-model RL agents can master Atari Pong on paper — but freeze their world models and watch closely: the ball vanishes, bounces wrong, or phases through the paddle.

flashcards.prompt: What does the Transfer Reliability Score (TRS) measure in Spatial Memory Agent?

choices.text: How well a stored lesson has actually helped on later retrievals
How confident the frozen VLM was when it produced the original answer
How semantically similar a lesson is to the current query

flashcards.explanation_html: TRS starts uniform and is calibrated from later retrieval outcomes, so it's an empirical track record. Semantic similarity is a separate signal — retrieval ranks on both combined.

flashcards.back_html: The VLM stays frozen. Learning happens by writing verified experience into a lesson memory and retrieving it at inference time, so nothing in the weights changes.

flashcards.prompt: Why does SMA need a verifiable environment during its learning phase?
flashcards.back_html: Lessons are distilled through verifier-guided reflection — the reward signal tells it which attempts were actually right, so it doesn't confidently store lessons drawn from its own mistakes.
